purpose: Teach: 織り/格子/三輪/面影/根強い/坊さん/悔い/実体験

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、家で、絶対、織り、絶対、お母さん、絶対、していたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young — do you remember? Your mother was always weaving at home. Seriously.
lines.style: Soft, searching gaze into the past. Gentle opening, voice reaching back decades. Pause before 'do you remember' — giving her time to meet him there. Warmth under the wistfulness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。実家の窓、本気で、絶対、格子、絶対、なってたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. The lattice windows in my family home — I still see them so clearly. Do you remember, dear?
lines.style: Voice lighting with recognition. Tender and present, not lost in memory but holding it close. Slight lean toward him. The cadence of someone who has carried these images her whole life.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、三輪、絶対、自転車、絶対、お父さん、絶対、孫に、絶対、買ってあげたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young — your father bought you a tricycle. Do you remember? He was so proud.
lines.style: Quieter now, voice holding both love and a kind of old grief. The words come slower, each one weighted. Slight catch before 'do you remember' — checking himself to be present with her.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お父さんに、本気で、絶対、若い頃の、絶対、面影、絶対、まだ、絶対、残っているわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And your father still has that same look in his eyes from back then. Do you see it, dear? It's still there.
lines.style: Warm certainty in her voice. She's noticing something in him right now. Soft, almost wondering — how the young face lives inside the older one. Reaching across the table toward him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家業の、絶対、根強い、絶対、お客様、絶対、たくさん、絶対、いてくださったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: The family business was thriving. So many loyal customers came to us. Do you remember those days?
lines.style: Voice taking on quiet pride. The weight of those years — busy, full, purposeful. Slight lift in 'thriving' and 'loyal' but then settling back into reflection. Slower tempo.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お寺の、本気で、絶対、坊さん、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、よく、絶対、お話、絶対、していたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather used to talk with the monks from the temple. They'd come often. Do you remember those conversations?
lines.style: Her voice softens with reverence. She's remembering something important, maybe spiritual. Not wistful but grounded — the monks mattered. Her pace slows for their names and her certainty on 'often' is steady.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんが、絶対、ばあさんに、絶対、もっと、絶対、言葉を、絶対、かけられなかった、絶対、悔い、絶対、残っているぞ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Your father... he always regretted not saying more to your grandmother. That weighs on him still. I want you to know this.
lines.style: Voice becomes urgent without raising in volume. Direct eye contact in the voice. This is not nostalgia — this is a request, almost a charge. Gravity on 'regretted' and 'weighs on him still.' The ending is firm, tender, serious.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんの、本気で、絶対、実体験、絶対、孫に、絶対、お話、絶対、しましょうね、あなた
lines.en: Your grandfather's life, his real experiences — let's tell them to your grandchildren someday, won't we?
lines.style: Gentle but purposeful. A shared mission now, not a memory. Her voice reaches toward the future while holding the past. Slight lift on 'someday' — hope. Warmth on 'won't we' — this is a partnership, not a request.
